title_en: Zhang Xitian v. Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Huasheng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., CSPC Pharmaceutical Group Zhongqi Pharmaceutical Technology (Shijiazhuang) Co., Ltd., and Jilin Province Yushuntang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of invention patent
ruling_gist_en: Article 11 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: 'After the grant of a patent for invention or utility model, except as otherwise provided in this Law, no entity or individual may, without the authorization of the patentee, exploit the patent, that is, may not manufacture, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product, or use the patented process, and use, offer to sell, sell, or import the product directly obtained by the patented process for production and business purposes.' According to the foregoing provision, in an infringement dispute involving a patent for a method of manufacturing a new product, the scope of protection of the method patent includes only the original product directly obtained by the patented method, and does not include subsequent products obtained after further processing of the original product.

full_text_en:
Zhang Xitian v. Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Huasheng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., CSPC Zhongqi Pharmaceutical Technology (Shijiazhuang) Co., Ltd., and Jilin Yushuntang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. — dispute over infringement of invention patent

【Ruling Summary】

Article 11 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "After the grant of an invention patent or utility model patent, unless otherwise provided for in this Law, no entity or individual may, without the authorization of the patentee, exploit the patent, i.e., may not, for production or business purposes, manufacture, use, offer to sell, sell, or import the patented product, or use the patented process, or use, offer to sell, sell, or import the product directly obtained by the patented process." According to the foregoing provision, in a case involving a dispute over infringement of a patent for a process for manufacturing a new product, the scope of protection of the process patent extends only to the original product directly obtained by using the patented process, and does not extend to subsequent products obtained after further processing of the original product.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2009) Min Ti Zi No. 84

The Retrial Applicant (Defendant at First Instance, Appellant at Second Instance): Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 276 Zhongshan West Road, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Wang Ruiqi, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Li Hongtuan, female, legal counsel of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., residing at Room 909, Building 2, Longxiang Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Agent ad litem: Guo Weiqin, female, employee of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., residing at Unit 34-2-401, Zhuoda Rose Garden, Huai'an Road, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

The Respondent (Plaintiff at First Instance, Appellee at Second Instance): Zhang Xitian, male, born on June 21, 1947, Han ethnicity, residing at No. 27-2 Lixin Lane, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Agent ad litem: Luo Yicheng, lawyer of Jilin Yifeng Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Hou Xujun, male, patent agent of Jinan Shunyuan Patent Agency Co., Ltd., residing at Unit 2-601, Building 1, No. 32 Qixinghe Road, Licheng District, Jinan City, Shandong Province.

Appellant at Second Instance (Defendant at First Instance): Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Huasheng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 276 Zhongshan West Road, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Cai Dongchen, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Li Hongtuan, female, legal counsel of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., residing at Room 909, Building 2, Longxiang Road, Haidian District, Beijing.
Agent ad litem: Li Guocong, male, employee of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., residing at No. 2 Zhongnan Road, Xinhua District, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Appellant at Second Instance (Defendant at First Instance): CSPC Zhongqi Pharmaceutical Technology (Shijiazhuang) Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 368 Xinshi North Road, Shijiazhuang City, Hebei Province.

Legal Representative: Cai Dongchen, Chairman of the Board.
Agent ad litem: Li Hongtuan, female, legal counsel of Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., residing at Room 909, Building 2, Longxiang Road, Haidian District, Beijing.

Defendant at First Instance: Jilin Yushuntang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd., domiciled at No. 417 Zhujiang Road, Changchun City, Jilin Province.

Legal Representative: Sun Minghai, Chairman of the Board.

The Retrial Applicant, Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Ouyi Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Ouyi), filed a petition for retrial with this Court against the civil judgment (2006) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 146 rendered by the Jilin High People's Court on November 21, 2006, in the dispute with the Respondent Zhang Xitian, the Appellants at Second Instance, Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group Huasheng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Huasheng), CSPC Zhongqi Pharmaceutical Technology (Shijiazhuang) Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zhongqi), and the Defendant at First Instance, Jilin Yushuntang Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Yushuntang), regarding infringement of invention patent. This Court rendered a civil ruling (2009) Min Shen Zi No. 2 on June 17, 2009, deciding to take up the case for retrial. This Lawfully formed a collegial panel and heard the case in an open session on May 5, 2010. The common agent ad litem of Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi, Li Hongtuan, the agent ad litem of Ouyi, Guo Weiqin, the agent ad litem of Huasheng, Li Guocong, and Zhang Xitian and his agent ad litem Hou Xujun appeared in court for the hearing. Yushuntang, being lawfully summoned, did not appear in court. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

In February 2005, Zhang Xitian filed a lawsuit with the Changchun Intermediate People's Court of Jilin Province (hereinafter referred to as the court of first instance), alleging: The plaintiff is the patentee of invention patent No. 00102701.8, titled "Resolution of amlodipine enantiomers," which is a process patent for manufacturing the new product levoamlodipine. The new drugs of levoamlodipine maleate and levoamlodipine maleate tablets were developed by Zhongqi, Huasheng produced levoamlodipine maleate (active pharmaceutical ingredient), Ouyi produced levoamlodipine maleate tablets (end product, trade name "Xuanning"), and Yushuntang sold the infringing products. The plaintiff requested the court to order: 1. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi to cease the infringing acts and publish an infringement notice regarding levoamlodipine maleate and levoamlodipine maleate tablets in national pharmaceutical media; 2. Yushuntang to cease selling the infringing products; 3. Zhongqi, Huasheng, Ouyi, and Yushuntang to bear all litigation costs, as well as appraisal fees, attorney fees, and other expenses incurred in this case.

The court of first instance found after trial that: On February 21, 2000, Zhang Xitian filed an application for an invention patent No. 00102701.8, titled "Resolution of amlodipine enantiomers" (hereinafter referred to as the patent-in-suit), which was granted on January 29, 2003. The patent-in-suit disclosed a method for manufacturing levoamlodipine, from which downstream products such as levoamlodipine maleate and levoamlodipine besylate could be further prepared. In June 2001, the third party Pfizer Research and Development Company (hereinafter referred to as Pfizer) was granted invention patent No. 95192238.6, titled "Resolution of enantiomers of amlodipine via diastereomeric tartrates" (hereinafter referred to as the '238 patent). Both of the above patents are process patents for manufacturing levoamlodipine. Before these patents, there was no industrial technology in China for manufacturing levoamlodipine.

The new drugs of levoamlodipine maleate and levoamlodipine maleate tablets were developed by Zhongqi, the active pharmaceutical ingredient levoamlodipine maleate was produced by Huasheng, and the end product levoamlodipine maleate tablets (trade name "Xuanning") was produced and sold by Ouyi. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi are all under the Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group and are independent legal entities. In 2004, the Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group promoted "Xuanning" on its website. According to the relevant webpages of the State Food and Drug Administration and its Center for Drug Evaluation, the levoamlodipine products manufactured domestically were levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets produced by Huasheng and Ouyi, as well as levoamlodipine besylate and its tablets produced by Zhang Xitian.

Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi submitted to the court of first instance a patent application publication with publication number CN1609102A, titled "A method for resolving optically active amlodipine," to prove that the method they used to manufacture the accused infringing products was different from the method of the patent-in-suit. Zhang Xitian filed an application with the court of first instance for expert appraisal, requesting an experimental test of the amlodipine resolution method described in that publication. The court of first instance entrusted the Fayuan Judicial Scientific Evidence Appraisal Center (hereinafter referred to as the Fayuan Center) to conduct the appraisal. The Fayuan Center issued an inspection report stating: "Under the same experimental conditions, using the method for producing amlodipine described in Example 1 of the invention patent publication CN1609102A, which is the most fully disclosed and has the highest enantiomeric excess, the experimental results showed a significant difference in enantiomeric excess from the description in the publication. Using the chemical method provided by invention patent CN1609102A, this experiment could not achieve the objective of resolving amlodipine."

The court of first instance held that: 1. Article 57, paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China (as revised for the second time) (hereinafter referred to as the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China) provides: "Where a patent infringement dispute involves a patent for a process for the manufacture of a new product, any entity or individual manufacturing the same product shall provide proof that the process used for its product is different from the patented process." The term "new product" as used in this provision refers to a product that has not been marketed in the domestic market before the patented product. Currently, only the plaintiff's levoamlodipine besylate and its tablets, and Ouyi's levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets are available in the domestic market, and the plaintiff's product was marketed earlier than Ouyi's product. Although Pfizer has been granted the '238 patent in China, its product has not yet been marketed in China. In addition, the plaintiff's levoamlodipine product was recognized by the former State Economic and Trade Commission as a national key new product for 2001 in May 2001, and was awarded the "Ninth Five-Year Plan" National Technology Innovation Excellent Project Award in June 2001 by the former State Economic and Trade Commission. Although the defendants argued that the plaintiff's product was not a new product, they failed to provide sufficient evidence to rebut this. Therefore, the patent-in-suit should be considered a process patent for manufacturing a new product. 2. Levoamlodipine, as a compound, cannot be directly consumed by consumers; it must be subjected to a salt-forming process with maleic acid, besylic acid, etc., to become levoamlodipine maleate, levoamlodipine besylate, etc., before it truly becomes a product. Therefore, the patent-in-suit can extend to the levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets produced by the defendants. 3. Pursuant to Article 57, paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi should provide evidence to prove that the method they used to manufacture levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets is different from the method of the patent-in-suit. According to the appraisal by the Fayuan Center, the patent method provided by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi could not achieve the objective of resolving amlodipine. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi failed to prove that their product manufacturing method was different from the method of the patent-in-suit and shall bear corresponding infringement liability according to law. 4. Zhang Xitian failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove the existence of Yushuntang's infringement. Accordingly, the court of first instance, pursuant to Articles 11, 57(2), and 60 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: 1. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi shall cease the acts of infringing the patent-in-suit. 2. Zhang Xitian's other claims are rejected. The case acceptance fee of RMB 1,000 and the appraisal fee of RMB 200,000 shall be borne by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi.

Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the Jilin High People's Court (hereinafter referred to as the court of second instance).

The court of second instance found after trial that the facts found by the court of first instance were correct.

The court of second instance held that the issues in dispute in this case were: 1. Whether the patent-in-suit is a process patent for manufacturing a new product; 2. Whether the scope of protection of the patent-in-suit extends to the levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets developed and produced by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi; 3. Whether the method used by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi to develop and produce the accused infringing products is identical or equivalent to the method of the patent-in-suit; 4. Whether the procedure for entrusting the appraisal by the court of first instance was legal, and whether the appraisal conclusion was correct and could prove infringement by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi; 5. Whether the trial of this case should be suspended; 6. Whether Zhongqi's research and development activities constituted infringement.

Regarding the first issue. According to the search results published on the webpages of the State Food and Drug Administration and its Center for Drug Evaluation regarding the patent and legal status of "levoamlodipine," currently, only levoamlodipine besylate and its tablets produced by Jilin Tianfeng Pharmaceutical Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Tianfeng), an entity implementing the patent-in-suit, and levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets produced by Ouyi are available in the domestic market. No other levoamlodipine drugs exist, and Pfizer's levoamlodipine product has also not been marketed in China. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi did not provide evidence to prove that before using the method of the patent-in-suit to produce levoamlodipine, other enterprises had already produced and sold similar drugs in the domestic market. Therefore, the claim by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi that the patent-in-suit is not a process patent for manufacturing a new product lacks factual and legal basis and is not supported.

Regarding the second issue. Levoamlodipine, as a compound, cannot itself directly become a product for consumer consumption. The patent-in-suit is a resolution method for levoamlodipine, and the product cannot be directly obtained by using this method. Only after the levoamlodipine compound undergoes a salt-forming process with maleic acid, besylic acid, etc., to become levoamlodipine maleate, levoamlodipine besylate, etc., does it truly become a product. Therefore, the above products should be considered products directly obtained by using the levoamlodipine resolution method. The patent-in-suit can extend to the levoamlodipine maleate and its tablets produced by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi.

Regarding the third and fourth issues. During the second instance, the court of second instance organized the parties and appraisal personnel to appear in court for questioning on the appraisal conclusion. Apart from procedural issues, Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi also argued that the appraisal conclusion was unscientific, and that it was normal that levoamlodipine could not be separated using only the patent documents, as there were many technical know-hows and control methods not recorded in the patent literature. The Fayuan Center's response was: 1. The Fayuan Center possesses the qualification for pharmaceutical appraisal. During the first instance, Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi once requested the Beijing Municipal Bureau of Justice to revoke the appraisal conclusion, but the Bureau of Justice replied in writing that the objection was unfounded. 2. The appraisal personnel had the corresponding qualifications and professional competence. The appraisal procedure was legal. The submitted materials had been inspected by the appraisal department, and the successful separation of levoamlodipine using Pfizer's patented method indicated that the equipment was in a stable state and the personnel operated correctly. 3. Regarding the claim by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi that only 40 ml of 2-butanone was used during the appraisal process, the Fayuan Center explained it was a clerical error and produced the original experimental records showing that 60 ml of 2-butanone was actually added. The court of second instance held that: 1. The Fayuan Center is an appraisal institution recognized and published by the Ministry of Justice and the Supreme People's Court, possessing qualifications for appraisal in forensic medicine, pharmacology, pharmaceutics, etc. The relevant appraisal personnel were experts in pharmaceutics and pharmacology, possessing appraisal qualifications. 2. Although there were some defects in the appraisal procedure, to reduce the litigation burden on the parties and without affecting the substantive resolution of the case, measures could be taken during the second instance to correct the procedural issues in the appraisal. If, after correction, the legality of the appraisal conclusion could be confirmed, there would be no need to re-organize an appraisal or remand the case for retrial. For this purpose, the court of second instance organized the parties to conduct investigations and challenges: (a) Regarding the failure of the court of first instance to notify Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi to appear in court when entrusting the appraisal. According to the first-instance case file, after the first attempt to select an appraisal institution failed, Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi had sent a letter to the court of first instance explicitly stating their disagreement with the appraisal. It was not that the court of first instance failed to notify them. (b) Regarding the submitted materials. The submitted materials were the amlodipine raw material purchased by Zhang Xitian. Since this material was not evidence, there was no issue of cross-examination. Although the submitted materials were not confirmed by both parties, the appraisal department, to ensure the fairness and scientific nature of the experiment, had inspected and confirmed the submitted materials, and successfully produced levoamlodipine using Pfizer's patented method. (c) Regarding the issue of applying for withdrawal. The court of second instance asked Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi whether they applied for withdrawal of the appraisal personnel, but Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi did not provide specific opinions on withdrawal, merely stating it was a procedural defect. 3. Regarding the appraisal conclusion. Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi argued that different experiments, different personnel, and control of stirring speed, temperature, etc., could all affect the experimental results, but they did not explain what specifically caused the failure to resolve amlodipine and how to achieve the resolution of amlodipine. The appraisal personnel were all experts in the field and obviously possessed the corresponding professional knowledge and operational skills. Since they could not achieve the objective of resolving levoamlodipine using the patented method provided by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi, and Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi failed to provide sufficient evidence to prove that their product manufacturing method was different from the method of the patent-in-suit, they should bear the consequences of failing to meet their burden of proof.

Regarding the fifth issue. Although the patent-in-suit had been partially declared invalid by the Patent Reexamination Board of the State Intellectual Property Office, both parties in that case had filed administrative lawsuits. At the same time, Ouyi had filed a civil lawsuit with the Shijiazhuang Intermediate People's Court of Hebei Province against Zhang Xitian and Tianfeng, alleging that they used the same method as Ouyi to produce levoamlodipine active pharmaceutical ingredient and finished drugs. This contradicts Ouyi's claims in this case. Therefore, the trial of this case should not be suspended.

Regarding the sixth issue. Since Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi are all under the Shijiazhuang Pharmaceutical Group, with Zhongqi responsible for research and development, Huasheng producing the active pharmaceutical ingredient, and Ouyi producing the finished drug, all three are indispensable in the process of producing levoamlodipine active pharmaceutical ingredient and finished drugs. Therefore, the claim that Zhongqi should not bear infringement liability is not supported.

The court of second instance, pursuant to Article 153, paragraph 1, item (1) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, ruled: The appeal is dismissed and the original judgment is affirmed. The first and second instance case acceptance fees of RMB 4,000 and the appraisal fee of RMB 210,000 shall be borne by Zhongqi, Huasheng, and Ouyi.

Ouyi Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of the second instance, applied to this Court for retrial on the following grounds: 1. The inspection report issued by the Fayuan Center was erroneous, and the courts of first and second instance erred in admitting it. 2. Ouyi Company had submitted evidence such as patent application documents, recorded production processes, and production records to prove that its product manufacturing method differed from the patented method in question; Ouyi Company also filed an application for on-site inspection, requesting the court of second instance to conduct an on-site inspection of the manufacturing method of the allegedly infringing product to demonstrate that it could produce levamlodipine using its own method, but the court of second instance disregarded this, relying solely on the inspection report from the Fayuan Center to conclude that Ouyi Company could not produce levamlodipine using its own method, constituting an error in fact-finding. 3. According to the method described in claim 1 of the patent in question, the resulting product is "(S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6" or "(R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6," which differs from the allegedly infringing product, and the patent in question does not qualify as a patent for a method of manufacturing a new product. The court of second instance erroneously used whether the product was marketed as the criterion for determining a "new product," and, without Zhang Xitian having proven that Ouyi Company also manufactured the above product, required Ouyi Company to bear the burden of proving that its product manufacturing method differed from the patented method, constituting errors in both fact-finding and application of law. 4. Ouyi Company's product manufacturing method significantly differs from the patented method and constitutes a different technical solution. The court of second instance extended the scope of protection of the patent in question to cover levamlodipine maleate and its tablets, which was also erroneous. Ouyi Company requested this Court to: 1. Set aside the civil judgment of the Changchun Intermediate People's Court, Jilin Province (2005) Chang Min San Chu Zi No. 36 and the civil judgment of the Jilin High People's Court (2006) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 146. 2. Declare that Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company did not infringe the patent in question. 3. Order Zhang Xitian to bear the appraisal fees and all litigation costs of this case.

Zhang Xitian argued in defense that: 1. The Fayuan Center is an appraisal institution recognized by the Ministry of Justice and the Supreme People's Court as having qualifications for drug and pharmacological appraisal, and the appraisers organized by the Fayuan Center were all experts in the field with the relevant professional knowledge and operational skills. Therefore, the court of original instance properly admitted the inspection report issued by the Fayuan Center. 2. Levamlodipine produced by the patented method is a new product, and Ouyi Company should bear the burden of proving that its product manufacturing method differs from the patented method. Experimental verification showed that Ouyi Company's claimed patented method could not produce levamlodipine; therefore, Ouyi Company should bear the consequences of failing to meet its burden of proof. 3. Ouyi Company's assertion that implementing its patented technology required skill and know-how lacked factual basis and scientific foundation. 4. Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company, without Zhang Xitian's permission, researched, manufactured, and sold levamlodipine maleate and its tablets for production and business purposes, and should bear liability for infringement.

Upon retrial, this Court found that the facts found by the courts of first and second instance were substantially true.

This Court further found the following facts:

(I) Facts concerning the patent in question

Claim 1 of the granted patent in question states: "1. A method for separating (R)-(+)- and (S)-(-)-isomers of amlodipine from a mixture, characterized by comprising the following reaction: in a chiral auxiliary, hexadeuterated dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO-d6) or an organic solvent containing DMSO-d6, reacting the mixture of isomers with a chiral resolving agent D- or L-tartaric acid to precipitate (S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6, or (R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6, wherein the molar ratio of amlodipine to tartaric acid is approximately 0.25." The specification of the patent in question states: "The process of resolving amlodipine is: dissolving amlodipine and tartaric acid separately in a chiral auxiliary, hexadeuterated dimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO-d6) or an organic solvent containing DMSO-d6, then stirring and mixing; amlodipine reacts with D- or L-tartaric acid to precipitate (S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6, or (R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate combined with one DMSO-d6. Methods for separating the precipitate include filtration, centrifugation, or decantation. Further treatment of the precipitate yields (R)-(+)-amlodipine or (S)-(-)-amlodipine. The mother liquor after removing the precipitate can be treated with 0.25 equivalents of tartaric acid of opposite polarity (e.g., if L-tartaric acid was used first, D-tartaric acid is now used) to precipitate the opposite polarity amlodipine and its tartrate and DMSO-d6 complex. ... The solvent used for recrystallizing the tartrate is an alcohol, such as methanol." Example 5 of the specification of the patent in question also describes a method for producing (S)-(-)-amlodipine besylate from (S)-(-)-amlodipine. In the patent in question, "(S)-(-)-amlodipine" refers to levamlodipine, and "(R)-(+)-amlodipine" refers to dextroamlodipine.

(II) Facts concerning Pfizer's Patent No. 238

Pfizer applied for Patent No. 238 on March 6, 1995, and was granted the patent on June 13, 2001, with the authorized publication number CN1067055C. Its specification states: "The present invention provides a method for separating (R)-(+)- and (S)-(-)-isomers of amlodipine from a mixture, comprising reacting the mixture with L- or D-tartaric acid in an organic solvent containing a sufficient amount of dimethyl sulfoxide to precipitate the DMSO solvate of (R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate or the DMSO solvate of (S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate, respectively." "The precipitated DMSO solvate can be further processed by several methods. Recrystallization from an organic solvent yields amlodipine tartrate free of DMSO. Further treatment with a base yields the free enantiomerically pure amlodipine isomer." Amlodipine referred to in Patent No. 238 is the same as amlodipine.

(III) Facts concerning Ouyi Company's patent application

On December 5, 2003, Ouyi Company filed an invention patent application No. 200310119335.7, titled "A method for resolving optically active amlodipine" (hereinafter "Patent No. 335"), which was published on April 27, 2005, with publication number CN1069102A, and granted on December 14, 2005. Claim 1 of the granted Patent No. 335 states: "1. A method for producing (S)-(-)-amlodipine, characterized by dissolving racemic amlodipine and L-(+)-tartaric acid in an organic solvent containing 2-butanone, reacting to produce a precipitate of (S)-(-)-amlodipine L-(+)-tartrate, filtering or centrifuging, then recrystallizing using ethanol, methanol, or isopropanol as solvent to obtain the solid, then adding dichloromethane, neutralizing with sodium hydroxide solution to obtain (S)-(-)-amlodipine." The specification of Patent No. 335 states: "Amlodipine is a calcium antagonist used clinically for treating hypertension and stable angina pectoris. Currently, clinically used amlodipine is mainly racemic, ... the main pharmacologically active component is (S)-(-)-amlodipine." "The other enantiomer, (R)-(+)-amlodipine, has activity in treating atherosclerosis. ... The method for preparing amlodipine enantiomers is mainly by resolving racemic amlodipine." Example 1 of the specification of Patent No. 335 describes a specific method for producing (S)-(-)-amlodipine, including the following steps: "Dissolve 5 g (0.012 mol) of amlodipine in 40 ml of 2-butanone, add 60 ml of a solution of 2-butanone containing 1.0 g (0.0066 mol) of L-(+)-tartaric acid, stir and react at room temperature for 1 hour, precipitate forms, filter, wash with a small amount of 2-butanone, obtain 2.1 g of solid. Distill the mother liquor to recover 2-butanone, recrystallize the solid obtained in ethanol, obtain 1.7 g of (S)-(-)-amlodipine L-(+)-tartrate. Add 18 ml of dichloromethane and 10 ml of 2N sodium hydroxide solution to the 1.7 g of (S)-(-)-amlodipine L-(+)-tartrate, stir and react for 30 minutes, let stand, separate the organic layer, add an appropriate amount of anhydrous sodium carbonate to dry, filter, wash the filter cake with a small amount of dichloromethane, concentrate the filtrate under reduced pressure, add an appropriate amount of n-hexane, stir to crystallize, filter, and vacuum dry overnight to obtain 1.2 g of (S)-(-)-amlodipine. The enantiomeric excess (ee) determined by chiral HPLC is 99.0%, yield 48%."

(IV) Facts concerning the inspection report issued by the Fayuan Center

The inspection report issued by the Fayuan Center states: "The testers in this experiment conducted repeat tests under the same conditions for the chemical reaction methods for producing amlodipine drugs described in Examples 1, 4, 5, and 8 of invention patent CN1067055C and Example 1 of invention patent CN1609102A. The test results are as follows: 1. Using the methods described in Examples 1, 4, 5, and 8 of CN1067055C, the test results were consistent with the descriptions in its specification, proving the reliability of the testers' experimental capabilities and raw materials and reagents. 2. Under the same test conditions, using the method described in Example 1 of invention patent CN1609102A, which is the most fully disclosed in its specification and has the highest enantiomeric excess, the test results showed significant differences in enantiomeric excess compared to the description in its specification. Using the chemical method provided by that invention patent, this test could not achieve the purpose of resolving amlodipine." The invention patent CN1609102A referred to in the report is Ouyi Company's Patent No. 335, and invention patent CN1067055C is Pfizer's Patent No. 238. The judicial appraisal license of the Fayuan Center indicates that its appraisal business scope includes forensic pathology appraisal, forensic clinical appraisal, forensic biological evidence appraisal, forensic toxicology appraisal, document forensic appraisal, trace forensic appraisal, forensic accounting appraisal, construction engineering forensic appraisal, and asset appraisal forensic appraisal, but does not include intellectual property forensic appraisal.

On March 3, 2006, the Fayuan Center issued an invoice for technical appraisal fees, with the amount stated as RMB 200,000. The original judgment erroneously determined the technical appraisal fee as RMB 210,000.

(V) Concerning evidence submitted by Ouyi Company regarding the method for manufacturing levamlodipine

During the first and second instances of this case, Ouyi Company submitted evidence including the published specification of Patent Application No. 335, the granted invention patent specification, the recorded production process filed with the State Food and Drug Administration, production records, an on-site inspection record issued by the Shijiazhuang Food and Drug Administration of Hebei Province, and the "Process Procedure for Levamlodipine Maleate SOP-MPP-W017 (00)," to prove that it manufactured levamlodipine using its own method and did not use the patented method. Comparing the published specification of Patent Application No. 335, the recorded production process, the production records, and the "Process Procedure for Levamlodipine Maleate SOP-MPP-W017 (00)," although the methods for manufacturing levamlodipine described in said evidence differ in some raw materials, dosages, specific reaction conditions, etc., they all use L-(+)-tartaric acid and 2-butanone as raw materials to resolve amlodipine to produce levamlodipine.

(VI) Facts concerning on-site inspection

During the second instance of this case, Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company jointly applied to the court of second instance for an on-site inspection on the grounds that implementing Patent No. 335 required certain experience, skills, and know-how, requesting that the court organize the parties and relevant technical experts to conduct an on-site inspection of the manufacturing method of the allegedly infringing product. The court of second instance did not conduct the on-site inspection. During the retrial of this case, Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, Ouyi Company, and Zhang Xitian all applied to this Court for an on-site inspection, requesting that this Court conduct an on-site inspection of the manufacturing method of the allegedly infringing product to verify whether levamlodipine could be produced according to Ouyi Company's Patent No. 335 method.

On March 23, 2010, judicial personnel of this Court, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem, and the agents ad litem of Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company jointly went to Ouyi Company's warehouse to collect on-site samples of the experimental raw materials purchased by Ouyi Company. Four samples were taken for each type of raw material, with one sample taken back by Zhang Xitian's agent for testing, one retained by Ouyi Company, and two retained by this Court for future reference. After sampling, with the parties present and without objection, the judicial personnel of this Court sealed the raw materials in a safe in the warehouse. Within the period specified by this Court, Zhang Xitian did not raise any objection to the raw materials.

From April 10 to 12, 2010, the judicial personnel of this Court, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem and two assistants, and the agents ad litem of Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company went to Ouyi Company to conduct the on-site test. After verifying that the raw materials were sealed intact and the parties had no objections, three staff members of Ouyi Company conducted three sets of nine amlodipine resolution tests in total according to the raw materials and proportions recorded in Example 1 of Patent No. 335. During the test, the staff gradually added 60 ml of 2-butanone solution to the amlodipine solution, stirring and reacting at a water bath temperature of 34 degrees Celsius. Thereafter, the staff combined the solids obtained from the nine resolution tests and combined them for recrystallization to obtain the final test product. Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem took on-site samples of the mother liquor, precipitate, and final product obtained from the test, taking four samples for each, with one held by Zhang Xitian and one by Ouyi Company, and two retained by this Court for future reference. After the test, with the parties confirming no errors, the remaining raw materials were sealed again. Ouyi Company tested the final product obtained from the on-site test and found it to be levamlodipine with a purity of 99.7% and an enantiomer content value of 99.4.

During the on-site test, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem raised the following objections regarding the steps of Ouyi Company's on-site test: 1. According to Example 1 of Patent No. 335, all 60 ml of the 2-butanone solution containing 1 g of L-(+)-tartaric acid should be added to the amlodipine solution, then stirred and reacted at room temperature for 1 hour. However, during the test, the staff gradually added the 60 ml of 2-butanone solution and stirred at a water bath temperature of 34 degrees Celsius. 2. Ouyi Company combined the solids obtained from the nine resolution tests and then performed subsequent recrystallization steps, whereas according to Example 1 of Patent No. 335, the solids obtained from each of the nine resolution tests should be recrystallized separately. Based on this, Zhang Xitian argued that the test method used by Ouyi Company differed from Example 1 of Patent No. 335 and could not prove that the resolution of amlodipine could be achieved according to Patent No. 335. After consultation between Ouyi Company and Zhang Xitian, Ouyi Company agreed to conduct a second test, where three staff members would each conduct an amlodipine resolution test and recrystallize the solids obtained from each test separately.

On April 23, 2010, the judicial personnel of this Court and Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem went to Ouyi Company for the second test. Upon inspection, the remaining raw materials from the first test were sealed intact, and Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem did not raise any objection. However, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem, on the grounds that the raw materials may not have been mixed evenly during the first test and that the raw materials had been kept by Ouyi Company throughout, and the raw materials used in the first test might not be consistent with the samples taken before the test, requested that the raw materials be sampled and tested again before the second test. Ouyi Company argued that Zhang Xitian and his agent's request for re-sampling and testing the raw materials was intended to delay the proceedings. If Zhang Xitian believed there was a problem with the raw materials used in the first test, he could take the remaining raw materials away for testing, and there was no need for a second test; if Zhang Xitian accepted the test raw materials, the second test could proceed. As the parties could not reach an agreement, the second test was not conducted. Zhang Xitian's agent did not take the remaining raw materials away for testing.

This Court holds that the focus of this case is: 1. Whether the allocation of the burden of proof by the court of original instance was correct; 2. Whether Ouyi Company's method for manufacturing levamlodipine falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question; 3. Whether the inspection report issued by the Fayuan Center can be admitted.

I. Whether the allocation of the burden of proof by the court of original instance was correct

Article 57, paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China provides: "In a patent infringement dispute involving an invention patent for a method of manufacturing a new product, the entity or individual manufacturing the same product shall provide proof that its product manufacturing method differs from the patented method." According to this provision, in such patent infringement disputes, the alleged infringer bears the burden of proving that its product manufacturing method differs from the patented method, which requires meeting certain prerequisites: that the patentee can prove that the product manufactured according to the patented method is a new product, and that the product manufactured by the alleged infringer is the same product as the product manufactured according to the patented method.

In determining whether a method patent is a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product, the product directly obtained by practicing the patented method shall be used as the basis. The so-called "product directly obtained by practicing the patented method" refers to the original product obtained by using the patented method, and does not include subsequent products obtained by further processing of the original product. According to claim 1 of the patent in question, although the title of the subject matter is "a method for separating (R)-(+)- and (S)-(-)-isomers of amlodipine from a mixture," based on the content recorded in claim 1, the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question are "(S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6" or "(R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6," the former being an intermediate for manufacturing S-amlodipine, not S-amlodipine itself; and the latter being an intermediate for manufacturing R-amlodipine, not R-amlodipine itself. Since before the filing date of the patent in question, the aforementioned intermediates were not known to the public domestically or abroad, it can be determined that the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question are new products, and the patent in question is a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product. Although Ouyi Company submitted Pfizer's Patent No. 238 to prove that the patent in question is not a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product, because Patent No. 238 and the patent in question use different chiral auxiliaries, DMSO and DMSO-d6 respectively, to resolve amlodipine, the intermediates formed in the process of manufacturing S-amlodipine or R-amlodipine under the two patented methods are not the same. Therefore, Patent No. 238 did not disclose the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question, and is insufficient to prove that the patent in question is not a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product.

Although the patent in question is a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product, for the burden of proof to shift to the alleged infringers Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company to prove that their product manufacturing methods differ from the patented method, the right holder Zhang Xitian must first prove that the products manufactured by the alleged infringers are identical to the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method. As previously discussed, practicing the method recorded in claim 1 of the patent in question directly yields "(S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6" or "(R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6." Although the evidence provided by Zhang Xitian can prove that Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company manufactured S-amlodipine maleate and its tablets, and that the manufacture of S-amlodipine maleate requires S-amlodipine as a raw material, he did not provide evidence to prove that Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company, in manufacturing S-amlodipine maleate and its tablets, also manufactured the intermediate product "(S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6." Therefore, the evidence provided by Zhang Xitian is insufficient to prove that the products manufactured by Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company are identical to the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question. In this case, the burden of proof should not be shifted to Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company to prove that their product manufacturing methods differ from the patented method.

Although the court of first instance correctly concluded that the patent in question is a patent for a manufacturing method of a new product, its identification of the product directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question as S-amlodipine was clearly erroneous. Because the court of first instance erred in identifying the product directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question, and under circumstances where Zhang Xitian did not provide sufficient evidence to prove that the products manufactured by Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company were identical to the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method, its conclusion that Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company bore the burden of proving that their product manufacturing methods differed from the patented method was also clearly erroneous.

2. Whether Ouyi Company's method of manufacturing S-amlodipine falls within the scope of protection of the patent in question

During the first and second instance proceedings of this case, Ouyi Company successively submitted evidence including the published specification of Patent Application No. 335 and the granted invention patent specification, the process flow records and production records filed with the State Food and Drug Administration, and the "SOP-MPP-W017 (00) Process Procedure for S-amlodipine Maleate," to prove that it used its own method to manufacture S-amlodipine and did not use the patented method in question. Zhang Xitian claimed that the method for manufacturing S-amlodipine recorded in the aforementioned evidence could not achieve the resolution of amlodipine or produce high-purity S-amlodipine, and submitted an inspection report issued by Fayuan Center. To verify whether Ouyi Company could produce S-amlodipine using its own method, this Court, upon the requests of Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, Ouyi Company, and Zhang Xitian, conducted an on-site inspection of Ouyi Company's method for manufacturing S-amlodipine. Ouyi Company conducted an on-site experiment according to the method for manufacturing S-amlodipine recorded in Patent No. 335. The experimental results showed that, using 2-butanone and L-(+)-tartaric acid as raw materials according to the method recorded in Patent No. 335, Ouyi Company achieved the resolution of amlodipine and produced S-amlodipine with a content of 99.7% and an enantiomeric excess value of 99.4. Zhang Xitan acknowledged the experimental results in court.

Although Zhang Xitian raised objections to certain experimental steps and raw materials used in Ouyi Company's on-site experiment, none of these objections are tenable. 1. Regarding the method of adding 60 ml of 2-butanone and the reaction temperature. Based on the facts found, the technical feature corresponding to the above step in claim 1 of Patent No. 335 is "dissolving racemic amlodipine and L-(+)-tartaric acid in an organic solvent containing 2-butanone, reacting to generate..." The corresponding technical feature in Example 1 is "adding a solution of 1.0 g of L-(+)-tartaric acid in 60 ml of 2-butanone, stirring at room temperature for 1 hour." None of these technical features limit the specific method of adding the 2-butanone or the specific reaction temperature. Ouyi Company's addition of the 60 ml of 2-butanone solution in portions during the on-site experiment, and its stirring reaction in a water bath at 34 degrees Celsius due to the lower ambient temperature on the day of the experiment, did not exceed the scope defined by the above technical features. Therefore, this objection by Zhang Xitian is untenable. 2. Regarding Ouyi Company's combination of solids obtained from nine resolution experiments for recrystallization during the on-site experiment. During the on-site experiment, Ouyi Company indeed combined the solids obtained from nine resolution experiments for recrystallization. After Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem raised an objection, Ouyi Company agreed to conduct a second on-site experiment, recrystallizing the solids obtained from each resolution experiment separately. However, under circumstances where the remaining raw materials were sealed and intact, Zhang Xitian requested re-testing of the experimental raw materials, preventing the second on-site experiment from proceeding. In fact, based on the facts found, the technical feature corresponding to recrystallization in Example 1 of Patent No. 335 is: "recrystallizing the obtained solid in ethanol," and the corresponding technical feature in granted claim 1 is: "then recrystallizing using ethanol, methanol, or isopropanol solvent." Therefore, Ouyi Company's combination of solids from nine resolution experiments for recrystallization did not exceed the scope defined by the above technical features. Moreover, according to common knowledge in the art, whether the solids obtained from resolution experiments are combined for recrystallization or recrystallized separately does not affect the ability to resolve S-amlodipine. Therefore, this objection by Zhang Xitian is also untenable. 3. Regarding the authenticity of the experimental raw materials. During the trial, Zhang Xitian questioned the raw materials used by Ouyi Company in the on-site experiment, claiming they differed from the sampled raw materials, and after testing samples such as precipitates obtained during the on-site experiment, the results significantly differed from his own comparative experiments. Thus, he suspected that Ouyi Company had used high-purity S-amlodipine as a raw material during the on-site experiment. In support of his claim, Zhang Xitian submitted his own comparative experiment report to this Court. In fact, after sampling the experimental raw materials purchased by Ouyi Company, the trial judges of this Court immediately sealed the raw materials on-site in the presence and with the acknowledgment of all parties. Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem did not object to the sampling and sealing of the raw materials. Before the on-site experiment began, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem inspected the sealed raw materials, the experimental site, and the experimental equipment. Only after confirming that the raw materials were intact and raising no objections did Ouyi Company unseal the raw materials for the experiment. During the experiment, Zhang Xitian's agent ad litem and two assistants supervised the entire process, and the agent ad litem raised no objections regarding the withdrawal of raw materials during that period. After the on-site experiment concluded, with no objections from any party, this Court sealed the remaining raw materials again. In summary, the sampling, sealing, use, and resealing of the experimental raw materials were all conducted under the joint supervision of all parties, sufficient to guarantee the objectivity and authenticity of the experimental raw materials. Zhang Xitian's challenge to the authenticity of the experimental raw materials, based solely on his own comparative experiment report, lacks both authenticity and scientific reliability. Therefore, Zhang Xitian's objection regarding the experimental raw materials is also untenable.

The results of Ouyi Company's on-site experiment corroborate with the evidence submitted by Ouyi Company, including the recorded process flow, production records, and the "SOP-MPP-W017 (00) Process Procedure for S-amlodipine Maleate." This can prove that Ouyi Company, using 2-butanone and L-(+)-tartaric acid as raw materials, can achieve the resolution of amlodipine and produce S-amlodipine. In comparison, claim 1 of the patent in question uses hexadeuterodimethyl sulfoxide (DMSO-d6) and D-tartaric acid as raw materials. The raw materials used by the two methods are neither identical nor equivalent. Therefore, Ouyi Company's method of manufacturing S-amlodipine does not fall within the scope of protection of the patent in question. During the trial, Zhang Xitian also acknowledged that the method using 2-butanone and L-(+)-tartaric acid as raw materials to manufacture S-amlodipine differs from the patented method, but merely claimed that it is impossible to produce S-amlodipine using that method. However, the on-site experimental results proved that high-purity S-amlodipine can be produced using that method. Therefore, Ouyi Company's defense that it manufactured S-amlodipine according to its own method is established. The court of first instance determined that Ouyi Company could not produce S-amlodipine using its own method and, based on that, concluded that Zhongqi Company, Huasheng Company, and Ouyi Company had infringed Zhang Xitian's patent rights. This determination clearly lacks factual basis.

It should also be noted that, according to Article 11 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, the scope of protection of a method patent can only extend to the product directly obtained by practicing that patented method, i.e., the original product obtained by using the patented method, and cannot extend to subsequent products obtained by further processing of the original product. As previously discussed, after practicing the method defined in claim 1 of the patent in question, the direct product obtained is "(S)-(-)-amlodipine D-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6" or "(R)-(+)-amlodipine L-tartrate bound to one DMSO-d6." The S-amlodipine maleate, S-amlodipine maleate tablets, and S-amlodipine produced by Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company are all subsequent products obtained by further processing of the above products and do not belong to the products directly obtained by practicing the patented method in question. Therefore, the scope of protection of the patent in question cannot extend to S-amlodipine, S-amlodipine maleate, or its tablets. The determination of "the product directly obtained by practicing the patented method" is unrelated to whether that product can be directly consumed by consumers. The court of first instance, on the grounds that "S-amlodipine, as a compound, cannot itself become a product for direct consumer consumption... the patent in question is a method for resolving S-amlodipine, and a product cannot be directly obtained by that method; only after the S-amlodipine compound undergoes a salt-forming process with maleic acid, benzenesulfonic acid, etc., to become S-amlodipine maleate or S-amlodipine besylate, does it truly become a product," extended the scope of protection of the patent in question to the S-amlodipine maleate and its tablets produced by Huasheng Company and Ouyi Company. This application of the law was also clearly improper.

3. Whether the inspection report issued by Fayuan Center can be admitted

As stated above, Ouyi Company has successfully produced S-amlodipine according to the method of Patent No. 335, and the on-site experimental results are sufficient to prove that the conclusion of the inspection report issued by Fayuan Center is erroneous. Therefore, Ouyi Company's retrial ground that this inspection report cannot be admitted is established, and this Court supports it. In fact, when conducting chemical experiments, the experimenter's experience and mastery of operational skills and know-how can substantially affect the experimental results. For example, in this case, Ouyi Company's Example 1 of Patent No. 335 only provided a relatively general description of the recrystallization step as "recrystallizing the obtained solid in ethanol." However, during the on-site experiment, Ouyi Company's staff actually observed and performed the recrystallization step with care and attention to detail. Therefore, although the appraisers organized by Fayuan Center could not produce S-amlodipine according to Patent No. 335, this is insufficient to conclude that Ouyi Company also could not produce S-amlodipine using that patented method. The court of first instance ignored the substantial impact that the experimenter's experience, skills, and know-how might have on the experimental results. Under circumstances where Ouyi Company explicitly stated that it possessed certain experience, skills, and know-how in implementing Patent No. 335, the court of first instance disregarded Ouyi Company's request to have its own staff conduct the experimental operations and readily admitted the inspection report from Fayuan Center, leading to an erroneous judgment.

In summary, the judgment of the original instance contained errors in both fact-finding and application of law and should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 11 and Article 57, Paragraph 2 of the Patent Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 186, Paragraph 1 and Article 153, Paragraph 1, Items (2) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the judgment is as follows:

1. The Civil Judgment (2006) Ji Min San Zhong Zi No. 146 of the Jilin High People's Court and the Civil Judgment (2005) Chang Min San Chu Zi No. 36 of the Changchun Intermediate People's Court, Jilin Province, are reversed.

2. The claims of Zhang Xitian are dismissed.

The court costs of first instance, RMB 1,000; the court costs of second instance, RMB 3,000; and the appraisal fee, RMB 200,000, totaling RMB 204,000, shall be borne by Zhang Xitian.

This judgment is final.
